newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Feb budget gap down, target to be bettered.
newsitem.headline: Canada Feb budget gap down, target to be bettered.

text.p: Canada said on Monday its federal budget deficit fell to C$485 million in February from C$2.31 billion a year earlier and progress was so strong that the government would better even its new full-year targets.
For the fiscal year to date, April to February, the deficit totalled C$7.83 billion, down from C$23.28 billion in the same period a year earlier, the Finance Department said.
"The financial results to the end of February 1997 confirm that the final outcome will be below C$19 billion," it added.
The February budget had said the gap would be no higher than C$19 billion, down from an original C$24.3 billion goal.

Only March is left in the 1996-97 fiscal year. Economists say unusual factors for March such as tax refunds, combined with technical end-of-year adjustments, make it difficult to extrapolate the 12-month deficit from partial figures.
But they have been saying -- now supported by the Finance Department -- it was clear the gap would end up less than C$19.0 billion.
The figures were released in the Finance Department's monthly Fiscal Monitor.
Budgetary transactions (in billions of dollars)
Program spending -8.82 -9.13 -91.76 -96.54
Operating balance +3.09 +1.38 33.13 19.38
Public debt charges -3.57 -3.69 -40.95 -42.66
Fin requirements (ex forex) +2.77 -0.09 +0.97 -15.16
Forex transactions -0.47 +0.95 -5.47 -1.56
(Note: Positive numbers indicate net source of funds. Negative numbers indicate net requirement for funds.)

The department said much of the increase in budgetary revenues for February reflected the timing of receipts and one-time factors. Personal income-tax collections were up C$0.7 billion, primarily due to the timing of receipts between February 1997 and March 1997, it said.

For the year to date, it said about C$5 billion of the C$9 billion increase in budgetary revenues was attributable to one-time factors, with the result that the underlying year-over-year increase in revenues was about 3.5 percent. It said this was in line with the 1996 increase in nominal income of 2.8 percent.

Personal income tax collections for the year to date were up by C$3.5 billion, and half of this it said related to taxes paid on filing, net of refunds, and on quarterly installmant payments. It said more taxpayers were required to make tax installment payments on income not subject to withholding.

It also said sales and excise taxes rose by 16.2 percent or C$1.0 billion largely because of a classification change related to the air transport tax, but since this affected both revenues and program spending, the deficit was unaffected.

Non-tax revenues for the fiscal year to date rose 23.5 percent, or C$1.3 billion, more than accounted for by the proceeds from the sale of the Air Navigation System and the inclusion of gains from introducing a two-dollar coin.

It said the financial requirements, excluding foreign exchange transactions, provided the government with a net source of funds of about C$1 billion, due to the improvement in the deficit and a somewhat higher net source of funds from non-budgetary transactions.
((Reuters Ottawa Bureau 613-235-6745))
